title: Compare an entire nonlinear scalar sector independently of shear amplitude
statement: Let kappa=2pi,E=span{e1 sin/cos(kappa x2),e2 sin/cos(kappa x1)},b(t) in E,b(0)=0. For f=b_t+nu kappa^2 b and initial V0+e3 phi with V0 in E and arbitrary mean-zero phi in L2(T2), exact full 2.5D solution is b+exp(-nu kappa^2 t)V0+e3 S_V0. Comparing scalar solution driven by the actual planar velocity to S_b driven by b gives ||S_V0-S_b||2<=||V0||2||phi||2 sqrt(t/nu), by divergence-free cancellation, scalar dissipation and ||V0||infinity<=sqrt(2)||V0||2. This is finite-amplitude, infinite-dimensional, not a Taylor approximation. With rational |lambda-nu kappa^2|<=zeta and f=b_t+lambda b, calibration r=(lambda-nu kappa^2)integral exp(-nu kappa^2(t-s))b(s)ds remains in E. If h=h_parallel+e3 h3, h_parallel in E, ||h||LinfinityL2<=eta, compare against scalar driven by b with SAME h3: error<=(||V0||2+eta t+zeta integral_0^t||b||2)(||phi||2+eta t)sqrt(t/nu). Four fixed rational spatial actuators suffice for this restricted comparison. It neither suppresses surviving E modes nor controls arbitrary 3D disturbances.
